Listen to this article Share Ibrahim Babangida and Abdulsalami Abubakar, former heads of state, have given President Bola Tinubu’s administration positive assessments, with Babangida reaffirming his support for the President’s re-election in 2027, while Atiku Abubakar, former vice president, has criticised Tinubu’s economic performance. Advertisement Advertisement Also, Babatunde Fashola, former Lagos State governor, has dismissed emerging opposition coalitions, predicting that they would fail to defeat the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections. Babangida and Abdulsalami expressed their positions on Thursday when a presidential delegation led by Femi Gbajabiamila, Chief of Staff to the President, visited them at their separate residences in Minna, Niger State. Speaking after a closed-door meeting with Babangida, Gbajabiamila said the former military leader was pleased with Tinubu’s performance and wished him success at the polls. “He is very happy with what Mr President is doing. He is very happy with his work, and he continues to support him and wishes him all the very best and the best of luck in the forthcoming elections,” Gbajabiamila said. Read also: Gov Abdulrazaq rallies support for Tinubu’s re-election, targets 35 APC seats in Kwara Advertisement Abdulsalami, speaking on behalf of the National Peace Committee, also said, “So far, so good. I think the President has done a good job.” He, however, urged Nigerians to prioritise peace ahead of the elections, warning that “without peace, there will be no country, and if there is no country, there wouldn’t be an election.” Advertisement In a contrasting assessment, Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, accused Tinubu’s administration of worsening the cost-of-living crisis through rising energy and production costs. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, his Director of Strategic Communication, Atiku cited reports that 11 listed manufacturing companies spent N842 billion on energy in the first nine months of 2026. Advertisement Advertisement “N842 billion is the energy bill of only 11 companies in nine months,” he said. Atiku argued that high electricity costs were pushing up cement prices and making housing increasingly unaffordable. Atiku also challenged the administration’s claim of delivering more than 26,000 housing units, demanding a breakdown of inherited projects, completed houses and occupied homes. Meanwhile, Fashola, speaking at the campaign kick-off of his support group in Lagos, compared the APC’s 2013 merger with previous political alliances, insisting that emerging opposition coalitions would fail. “All of the alliances you have seen on the horizon now will fail too, with your votes,” he declared. The rally also launched a mobilisation initiative to recruit 10,000 volunteers for Tinubu’s re-election and the election of Obafemi Hamzat, Lagos deputy governor and APC candidate as the state’s next governor.
